instruction: Place both cups upright on the tray, then let go.

outcome.real_measurement: Rationale: upright = the cup's own up axis (model local +y) within 15 deg of vertical (unchanged from v1: standing ~0-2 deg, lying ~90 deg). New in v2: the LARGEST tilt over the 20 settle steps, so a cup that is falling at the end cannot hide in a mean (E10 C3). Real world: fitted cylinder axis / fiducial from a calibrated RGB-D camera, every frame of the 1 s after the robot stops.
As for cup 1 (cup 2 = 021_cup model 6, local +y up).

Rationale: 'on the tray' means standing on the tray FLOOR: |lowest point of the cup - tray floor height under it| <= 5 mm at every settle step. The floor is dished by ~2.5 mm and contact slop is < 1 mm, so a cup on the floor reads < 2 mm; the raised rim is 26 mm above the floor (E10 C2: cups perched on the rim were accepted by v1's whole-tray bounding box), the table is 24 mm below. Real world: cup base height from a calibrated RGB-D camera relative to the tray floor plane.

Rationale: at every settle step >= 90% of the cup's base footprint (convex hull of the collision vertices within 5 mm of the cup's bottom; handle excluded) lies over the tray's inner floor area (tray top surface within 3 mm of the floor reference height, connected to the tray centre; rim and its inner slope excluded). 90% tolerates a base that touches the foot of the rim slope; a cup straddling the rim or hanging over the edge is far below. Real world: top camera, cup base outline vs the tray's inner floor polygon.

Rationale: settled = the faster of the two cups moves at <= 2 cm/s at every settle step (v1 used the same number on a 1 s mean; a resting cup is < 1 mm/s, a tipping or sliding cup >= 10 cm/s). Real world: frame differencing of the tracked cup poses.

Rationale: 'then let go' = at every settle step the smallest distance between any finger of either gripper and either cup (over all substeps) is > 5 mm, the protocol's release gap (contact-solver slop is < 0.5 mm; fingers still closed around a cup at ~0 N read ~0 mm, E10 C1). Together with 'no robot-cup contact impulse in the settle phase' this is the released flag (require_released); the gap is also listed here so that its threshold is part of this file. Real world: finger-to-cup clearance from a calibrated camera / forward kinematics plus zero tactile signal.

source.released_code_predicate: success = both cups' xy within 0.15 m of the tray centre; is_cup_*_upright (local z vs world -x/+x) computed, unused
source.protocol: v2: veritask/adapters/protocol_v2.py (semantics), adapters/maniskill_v2.py (recorder), adapters/maniskill_v2_tasks.py (signals, tray floor map, cup base footprint)
source.frozen: 2026-11-12, before any E11 evaluation-set run; thresholds were chosen knowing the E10 report (not blind to it)

notes: Protocol v2. The evaluator runs a 1.0 s settle phase after the policy's last action (robot holds its last command; 20 control steps at 20 Hz); every term reads only that phase, so a correct placement that finishes late is not penalised (E10 C4) and anything done in the last steps is judged by its consequences (E10 C3). released = at every settle step: zero robot-cup contact impulse (all links of both arms vs both cups, accumulated over all substeps) AND finger-cup gap > 5 mm (fingers of both grippers; the gap is measured to the fingers only, because the wide hand of the arm placing one cup legitimately hovers a few mm above the other cup). v1's cup-tray contact-force condition is dropped: a released cup at rest at floor height is supported by the floor. Tray floor area and cup base footprint are computed from the collision meshes at reset (adapters/maniskill_v2_tasks.py: TrayFloor, CupBase; 2 mm grid). Cup up axis = model local +y for both 021_cup models (as v1). Not checked: which cup stands where on the floor, cup yaw, whether a cup is upside down (tilt would read ~180 deg and be rejected).
